newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey mulling Cypriot joint military base.
newsitem.headline: Turkey mulling Cypriot joint military base.

text.p: Turkey is considering setting up a military base in northern Cyprus that would for the first time combine Turkish and Turkish Cypriot forces on the island, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Friday.

Anatolian said officials were working on the base plan as part of an accord between Ankara and Turkish Cyprus to be signed next week during a visit to Turkey by Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash. He is due in Ankara on Monday.

"The possibility of establishing a Turkish-TRNC military base on the island is the most sensitive point of work being conducted jointly by the foreign ministry and the general staff," the agency said.
About 30,000 Turkish troops are kept in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which only Ankara recognises, as well as 4,000 Turkish Cypriot soldiers.

Turkey has said it would increase its close support for the Turkish Cypriots in response to a decision by the Cyprus government in the Greek Cypriot-controlled south to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles. Ankara has threatened to use force to halt the deployment.
The agency did not say which branch of the military services any joint base would belong to.
Turkish officials are investigating whether a joint forces base would negatively affect Turkey's status as a guarantor of the island under a 1960 agreement with Greece and Britain.
"Turkey's role as guarantor of the island must not be harmed by any step that might be taken," the official said.
Turkey invaded the northern third of Cyprus in 1974 in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Athens.
